LESSON: WRITING 2.3.1 SOCIAL WRITING – CARDS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards, part of Strand 2 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we present cards to people? 2. How can we make cards more appealing when designing them?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the key components of a card for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. design a card (invitation card, appreciation card, congratulatory car

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. advocate for the role of social writing in enhancing communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the key components of a card for information,

   Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. design a card (invitation card, appreciation card, congratulatory car

   Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. for effective communication,

   Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. advocate for the role of social writing in enhancing communication.

   Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to collect sample cards from online and print sources,

2. study the cards to identify the key message passed,

3. identify the features of the cards,

4. work with peers to design a thank you card, congratulatory card and invitation card,

5. display the cards in the class gallery for peer review,

6. use a digital device to create a variety of e-cards (invitation, appreciation, congratulatory cards),

7. present the designed e-cards to the class for peer review. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to collect sample cards from online and print sources,
2. study the cards to identify the key message passed,
3. identify the features of the cards,
4. work with peers to design a thank you card, congratulatory card and invitation card,
5. display the cards in the class gallery for peer review,
6. use a digital device to create a variety of e-cards (invitation, appreciation, congratulatory cards),
7. present the designed e-cards to the class for peer review. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner works jointly with peers to present the designed e-cards to the class for peer

review.

• Creativity and Imagination: This is developed as the learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creativity by working with

peers to design a thank you card, congratulatory card and invitation card.

Values:
• Love: This is developed as the learner respects others when designing a thank you card, congratulatory card and invitation

card.

• Respect: The learner accommodates diverse opinions when presenting the designed e-cards to the class for peer review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

ICT: This is promoted as the learners use a digital device to create a variety of e-cards.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the skill of designing cards to the concept of arts in Creative Arts and Sports.
